name: Master Varenne of the Six Forges
lines: Fire is the first of the forges: it burns, it lights the dark and it makes steel.
Water slows what it touches and mends what is hurt, and it always comes back.
Earth stands: it knocks back whatever strikes it and wards whoever stands on it.
Air goes through: its arrows pass on, its spears come back, and its mantle flies.
Storm leaps: a blow struck with it runs on to the next foe and the next.
Life mends: what is struck with it gives back strength, and its wearer heals.
Ember vents on Mars and Mercury
Pearl pools in Neverland and a frozen spring on Pluto
Root-veins on the Moon and in the Underdark
Wind-worn spires on Veyar and in Neverland
Stormglass shards on Venus
Greenheart blooms in the Greenwold and at the North Pole
Cinderbrand, the Ember Blade
F swings it: a wave of flame runs out ahead of you. In Ironfray it burns what it strikes and scorches all round.
The Pyreheart Staff
F looses a ball of fire that bursts where it lands. In Ironfray the burst burns everything near.
Forgefall, the Magma Maul
F brings it down: fire bursts all round you. In Ironfray it hurls foes back and scorches the ground.
F raises a ring of flame round you. In Ironfray it turns blows aside and burns whoever strikes close.
Emberplate of the Six Forges
Worn: a breastplate and pauldrons of ember-steel. Fire relics strike twice as hard; in Ironfray it wards off blows.
The Circlet of the Ever-Coal
Worn: a warm, steady ember-light shines round you wherever you go.
The Mantle of Rising Ash
Worn: you drift down as softly as ash. No fall hurts you.
Worn: you walk and run a third as fast again.
Tidefang, the Deepwater Trident
F casts a wave that breaks where it lands. In Ironfray the wave slows everything it washes over.
F looses an arrow of rain. In Ironfray it passes through two foes and slows them.
The Staff of the Deep Current
F sends a current of water ahead. In Ironfray it reaches far and drags foes slow.
Brine-edge, the Pearl Dagger
A dagger of pearl and sea-steel. F: a quick cut of brine. In Ironfray every cut mends you a little.
Tideplate of the Drowned Kings
Worn: plate of sea-steel and mother-of-pearl. Water relics strike twice as hard; in Ironfray it wards off blows.
Worn: a soft sea-blue light shines round you wherever you go.
The Mantle of the Deep Tide
Worn: in Ironfray you mend quickly between blows, as the tide comes back.
Worn: you walk and run three tenths as fast again.
Mountainheart, the Quake Hammer
F brings it down and the ground heaves all round you. In Ironfray it throws foes far back.
The Bulwark of Deepstone
F sets a wall of stone round you. In Ironfray it turns most blows aside.
A long spear that reaches further than any. F: roots burst up where it points. In Ironfray it holds foes slow.
The Jade Blade of the Deep Roads
F swings it: stones leap up ahead of you. In Ironfray it knocks foes back.
Stoneplate of the Mountain Halls
Worn: plate of stone-steel set with jade. Earth relics strike twice as hard; in Ironfray it wards off blows.
Worn: a steady jade light shines round you wherever you go.
The Mantle of the Cliffside
Worn: in Ironfray blows land softer on you, as on stone.
Worn: you walk and run a quarter as fast again.
Galewing, the Sky Bow
F looses an arrow of wind. In Ironfray it flies true and passes through three foes.
Skyreach, the Returning Spear
F throws it on the wind, and the wind brings it back. In Ironfray it passes through two foes.
Whisperwind, the Breath Dagger
The quickest blade there is. F: a cut like a gust. In Ironfray it strikes almost as fast as you can press.
The Staff of the Wild Gale
F calls a gale ahead of you. In Ironfray it hurls foes away.
Galeplate of the High Eyrie
Worn: light plate as pale as the sky. Air relics strike twice as hard; in Ironfray it wards off blows.
The Cloudcrest Circlet
Worn: a soft white light shines round you wherever you go.
The Mantle of the High Wind
Worn: you can fly. Space to rise, C to come down.
Worn: you walk and run six tenths as fast again.
Thunderclap, the Storm Maul
F brings it down with a roll of thunder. In Ironfray the blow leaps on to four more foes.
Stormcaller, the Lightning Spear
F calls a line of lightning from its point. In Ironfray it leaps from foe to foe.
F swings it: sparks run out ahead. In Ironfray each blow leaps on to two more foes.
The Bow of Rolling Thunder
F looses a bolt of lightning. In Ironfray it leaps on to two more foes.
Stormplate of the Tempest Lords
Worn: dark plate veined with violet light. Storm relics strike twice as hard; in Ironfray it wards off blows.
The Crown of the Gathering Storm
Worn: a steady violet light shines round you wherever you go.
The Mantle of the Tempest
Worn: you ride the storm wind and can fly. Space to rise, C to come down.
Worn: you walk and run half as fast again.
The Evergreen Staff
F calls up a ring of green light that mends. In Ironfray it heals you whole in a breath.
F looses a spray of thorns. In Ironfray they slow whatever they strike.
F swings it: petals and green light run ahead. In Ironfray every blow mends you.
F raises a dome of leaves round you. In Ironfray it turns blows aside and mends you as you strike.
Barkplate of the Elder Grove
Worn: plate of living heartwood bound in gold. Life relics strike twice as hard; in Ironfray it wards off blows.
Worn: a soft green light shines round you wherever you go.
The Mantle of the Greenwood
Worn: in Ironfray you heal steadily, even in the thick of it.
This stone is black with old burning, and warm to the touch, though the rocks round it are cold. There is a gap under it, just wide enough for a hand.
Reach under the stone
On the red world, where the great mountain throws no shadow at noon, a stone stays warm that the Sun has long forgotten.
a coal that never cooled
Pressed into the dust is a lump of coal with a faint red heart. It has burned here for longer than anyone has walked this world.
Nearest the Sun, on the side away from my Hall, a coal has burned in the dust since before the first forge was lit.
a shell half buried in the sand
A great spiral shell lies half buried, pointing inland. When you lean close you hear the sea in it, though the sea is behind you.
In the land of the second star, a shell that should lie on the shore points inland. Listen to it.
A small pool, frozen hard. Under the ice something dark-blue moves very slowly, like cloth in a current.
On the coldest world, a pool has frozen over something that still moves with the tide.
a crack in the cavern floor
A crack in the floor runs straight as a rule, and the stone either side of it hums very faintly.
Prise the crack open
Under the world, where the dwarves dug deepest, a crack in the floor hums like a struck anvil.
a ring of pale stones
Seven pale stones sit in a perfect ring, too neat for chance. The dust inside the ring has never been walked on.
Brush the dust from the middle
On the Moon, a ring of seven pale stones keeps a crown no foot has touched.
a crystal that whistles
The wind whistles through one crystal and not the others. There is a hollow in its root, worn smooth.
Reach into the hollow
On Veyar, one crystal whistles when the others are silent. What sings there is a bow.
a feather caught on a rock
A long grey feather is caught on a rock, pinned flat by a wind that has dropped, high above the clouds.
In the city above the clouds, a wind dropped long enough to pin a feather to a rock, and never rose again.
a rod of fused glass
A rod of glass stands out of the ground where lightning once struck, still faintly warm. It is hollow.
Draw out what is inside
Where the lightning on Venus struck one place twice, the glass it made is hollow.
a black rock that hums
A black rock hums like a storm a long way off. The dust round it stands up a little, as hair does before lightning.
Turn the rock over
In the city among the greatest world's clouds, at its far edge, a black rock hums with a storm that never comes.
a sapling that never grows
A sapling no taller than your knee, with leaves greener than anything round it. Its roots are wound round something straight and smooth.
Ease the roots apart
In the Greenwold, a sapling has stayed small for a hundred summers, holding something in its roots.
a patch of green in the snow
A patch of moss as green as summer, in the middle of the snow. Under it, folded, something soft.
At the North Pole, past the pines, a patch of summer green lies in the snow.
The Shrine of Fire
A ring of black basalt round a steady flame that burns on nothing.
The Shrine of Water
A basin of white stone, always full, though no water runs to it.
The Shrine of Earth
A standing stone set with jade, warm as a hearthstone.
Three tall pale stones, and a wind that blows only between them.
The Shrine of Storm
An iron spire with a steady violet light caught at its tip.
The Shrine of Life
A ring of standing stones round a tree that is always in blossom.
A pool of tidepearls
A root-vein in the stone
A shard of stormglass
A greenheart bloom
Vellamar on Jupiter
Lumenreach in the Heavens
Master Varenne of the Six Forges
Welcome to the Six Forges. Mind the Ember Forge, it bites. What brings you to my anvil?
Brannoc Coalhand, smith of the Ember Forge
Stand back a pace, friend. She's hungry today.
Ysolde Tidewright, smith of the Tide Forge
Listen. You can hear the tide in the quench.
Durrik Stonebrow, smith of the Stone Forge
Hmph. Mind the anvil. It's older than your great-grandmother.
Sefa Lightwind, smith of the Gale Forge
Hold onto your hat! The bellows are in a mood.
Corvane Ashgrey, smith of the Thunder Forge
Quite safe. The storm is in the glass, and the glass is mine.
Mother Elowen, smith of the Green Forge
Come in, come in. Mind the seedlings.
